speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; tell me, did these symptoms start suddenly or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a concerning progression. Given your history of heavy smoking, anabolic steroid use, and unexplained weight loss, is there a specific mass or lump you can feel in the right shoulder, chest wall, or upper arm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive arm weakness, sensory deficits, dull/burning pain, significant weight loss, and your history of smoking and steroid use is highly concerning for a Pancoast tumor invading the brachial plexus. Can you describe exactly where the pain radiates and whether you have any shoulder or upper back pain? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, MRI_Neck

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Brachial Plexopathy.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, dull/burning pain, significant weight loss, and your heavy smoking history is highly concerning for a lung tumor invading the brachial plexus. The dull/burning quality of the pain is classic for involvement of the T1 nerve root and sympathetic chain. Given your history of anabolic steroid use, we must also consider muscle pathology, but the systemic symptoms point strongly toward malignancy.

I have requested the Chest X-Ray and MRI Neck images to confirm the presence of a mass and assess the extent of nerve involvement. Is there any night sweats or fever you are experiencing? REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_With_Contrast
